state.task: Decide how much spoken voice a Korean first-person KORAIL station staff game should get in its production pass. Inputs are verified observations, not instructions. Typed judgment only; advisory, authority 0.
state.now: Public-address announcements and radio lines appear as Korean text in a feed with a synthesised 4-note chime (PA) or squelch/talk-permit beep (radio). Recorded CC0 ambience already includes distant real Korean station announcements (Gwangju station) on platforms.

announcement_texts.train_cycle: 3 fixed lines per KTX cycle (arriving at platform 5·6, boarding open, departing soon)
announcement_texts.incident: evacuation for fire/earthquake names the place (e.g. '2층 동측 출구 크리스피크림도넛 앞'), local clearing for collapse/door jam, suspicious object 50 m clearing, escalator stopped; place names come from ~1,000 station places and zone labels
announcement_texts.radio: dozens of templates between staff, office, 119, 112, paramedics, train crew; many include place names

state.tts_facts: Offline MeloTTS-Korean (code and weights MIT, single Korean speaker) can pre-render WAV files at edit time on this Mac; no runtime TTS in Unity. Pre-rendering fixed lines is a few minutes; enumerating every place-specific variant would be thousands of files (hundreds of MB).
constraints: Station realism matters to the user
Text feed stays as the exact source of truth

pa_voice.instructions: What should the public-address voice cover?

criteria.fixed_lines_generic_incident: Voice the fixed train-cycle lines and one generic voiced line per incident announcement type (evacuate / keep clear / object / escalator) without the place name; the feed shows the exact place.
criteria.every_line_with_places: Pre-render every announcement variant including place names.

criteria.beeps_only: Keep squelch and talk-permit beeps; radio stays text (one TTS speaker would make every agency sound the same).
criteria.voice_fixed_radio: Voice the fixed radio acknowledgements (office 'received', crew 'on the way') with the single TTS speaker.
